rows.mechanism_and_interactions: The report separates three nonhuman bodies and marks its evidence as shown/stated/inferred/recalled: stationary plants act through shade, fruit, timber, humans and proxies, with seasons as clock/resource and neighbor shade competition; fungi split into network colonies (spread, trade, digest, signal; soil partners and fruiting) versus parasites (borrowed host senses, staged change, host agency/lifespan); place spirits couple environmental health to appearance, purification and human use, with day/night form hinges, ritual calendars and praise as distinct state/resource loops. Crossings retain differing bodies: plant shade/light, fungal host/network and place pollution/ritual are not one generic nature system. The “wood wide web” is explicitly contested, leading to a proposed trade/competition model rather than assumed cooperation.
